scholarships.title: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS)
scholarships.official_source: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR), A*STAR Graduate Academy

existing.description: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship (AGS) funds up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore, jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member, with research conducted at an A*STAR Research Institute. Support published for up to 4 years comprises full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment. Monthly allowance is a published matrix by track and residency status: AGS (STEM) $4,500 for Singapore Citizens, $4,100 for Singapore Permanent Residents and $3,600 for International Students; AGS (Specialised Tracks: Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) $6,200, $5,600 and $5,000 respectively.
eligibility: Study at an autonomous university in Singapore
Open to applicants of all nationalities. International Students applying must have completed or on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore Autonomous University (AU)
Obtained or on track to obtain at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline
Be in the last semester of their final studies to apply
Satisfy the criteria for and gain admission to a PhD programme in an autonomous university

Mid-Term AGS applicants: open to applicants of all nationalities; International Students applying must have completed or on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore Autonomous University (AU)
Mid-Term AGS applicants: obtained or on track to obtain at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline
Mid-Term AGS applicants: enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university and minimally completed at least 1 semester at the point of scholarship application
Mid-Term AGS applicants: on track to attain excellent academic standing for current degree
Mid-Term AGS applicants: good research potential and/or achievements
Mid-Term AGS applicants: current university supervisor to be at least 1 out of the 2 academic referees

The above eligibility criteria are not exhaustive. A*STAR may include additional selection criteria based on prevailing scholarship policies. These policies may be amended from time to time without notice.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants of all nationalities may apply, but international students must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore autonomous university, hold at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent, be in the last semester of final studies (full-term) or minimally one semester into a Singapore AU programme (mid-term), and satisfy PhD admission criteria at an autonomous university.
benefits: Specialised tracks in Semiconductor, Quantum and Computing offer a higher stipend than the AGS (STEM) track
Bond-free scholarship for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents

12-month overseas attachment opportunity (AGS scholars may be funded to conduct research at an overseas university/lab for a minimum period of 3 months and up to one year max, midway through the PhD, subject to supervisor endorsement and existing overseas collaborations)

AGS scholars can apply for the A*STAR International Fellowship (AIF), an overseas postdoctoral attachment of up to 2 years after PhD completion, fully funded by A*STAR; the AIF can be applied for within 4 years after completion of the PhD
Participation in Vista, A*STAR Graduate Academy's signature developmental programme series for scholars
coverage: Monthly sustenance allowance, inclusive of CPF contribution (where applicable)
Support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment
requirements: Before applying, identify and engage both an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member who are willing to collaborate on the project and co-supervise the PhD
In consultation with both supervisors, develop a research proposal that aligns with your research interests and contributes to Singapore's Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) ecosystem
Obtain endorsement from the A*STAR supervisor

Applicants need to apply separately to obtain admission to the intended partner university; the AGS award is conditional upon awardees obtaining confirmation of placement at one of the partner universities
AGS applicants should apply for university admission concurrently with the scholarship application

Scholars are required to satisfy the coursework requirements specified by the University conferring the PhD degree; graduation requirements shall be in accordance with the prevailing rules for the PhD degree applicable at the university
Please have your CV ready before creating your account to apply for the scholarship
documents: Curriculum vitae, ready before creating the application account
A description of the proposed research area
A brief summary of the proposed research project
Confirmation of the supervisor's willingness to co-supervise the project
The rationale for undertaking the project in collaboration with the university
Confirmation that the PhD research will be conducted, in whole or in part, at the relevant A*STAR Research Institute
application_method: Have your CV ready before creating your account to apply for the scholarship
Identify a research project and both supervisors (an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member)
Develop the research proposal in consultation with both supervisors
Apply for admission to the intended partner university concurrently with the scholarship application
Obtain endorsement from the A*STAR supervisor
Submit the online scholarship application with all supporting documents
Nominate at least 2 academic referees who will receive an auto-generated email with a link to complete an online referee report
Attend at least 2 rounds of interviews
Successful candidates are notified via email
existing.selection_notes: Referees can be academic referees from universities or supervisors/PIs whom you have worked with. There will be at least 2 rounds of interviews involving the senior management of the Biomedical Research Council or Science & Engineering Research Council, and researchers from A*STAR's Research Entities. The nomination of supervisor(s) has to be approved by A*STAR; in most cases the main and co-supervisors should hold at least the designation of Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist at an A*STAR RI. Final approval of the PhD supervisor(s), research project and university for successful applicants is subject to A*STAR's approval. A*STAR makes a holistic assessment of each application and takes into consideration factors such as achievements in science/maths related competitions and CCAs; prior research experience helps but is not mandatory. The application process typically takes about 5 months from submission of a complete application to notification of results.
existing.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates and Master's students at, or on track to graduate from, a Singapore autonomous university, and mid-PhD students already enrolled in a Singapore autonomous university, who want to do a research-intensive PhD at an A*STAR Research Institute. International students without Singapore Permanent Residence should be comfortable with a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company.
existing.notes: Bond-free for Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents. Foreigners who are non-SPRs must serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies, without commitment to any specific organisation; Singapore-based companies refer to local companies and international companies that have a base in Singapore and which is registered with the Accounting & Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA). The area of work should preferably be in Biomedical Sciences, Physical Sciences, Engineering or Computing and Information Sciences. Not deferrable within the 4-year funding period without approval: if you need more time to complete your PhD you will have to seek approval from A*STAR's management for your PhD extension. A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; fees involved in the lab should be borne by the university. All scholars need to seek A*STAR's written permission before changing your course of study/research project. Mid-term applicants receive the same terms of support as full-term AGS awardees from the point of the award, with retrospective payment for all tuition fees and/or any compulsory fees from Year 1 of study onward. All rates/allowances are subject to adjustments by A*STAR from time to time. A pre-application Master's degree is not required.
existing.application_period: Two cycles a year: 1 November to 1 February (outcomes from mid-April) and 1 June to 10 August (outcomes from mid-November). A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis.
existing.deadline_display: Application period: 1 November to 1 February & 1 June to 10 August. First application cycle opens on 1 November and closes on 1 February of the following year; second application cycle opens on 1 June and closes on 10 August of the following year.

scholarships.title: NUS Research Scholarship
scholarships.funding_label: Full Tuition Fee Waiver + Monthly Stipend
scholarships.official_source: NUS Graduate School, National University of Singapore

existing.description: The NUS Research Scholarship is awarded by the NUS Graduate School to outstanding graduate students for research leading to a higher degree at the National University of Singapore. It is open to PhD and Master's (Research) candidates of all nationalities, including Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents and international students, and covers a full waiver of tuition fees plus a monthly stipend. Stipend rates effective from 1 January 2026 are SGD 3,800 (Singapore Citizen PhD), SGD 3,400 (Permanent Resident PhD) and SGD 3,000 (international PhD) per month, and SGD 3,800, SGD 3,000 and SGD 2,900 respectively for Master's (Research) candidates. PhD scholars who pass the PhD Qualifying Examination may receive an additional stipend of up to SGD 500 per month, and international scholars must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirements.
eligibility: Qualification types: PhD Students and Master's (Research) Students
Nationalities: Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents, All International Students
Scholarship holders can pursue any graduate programme at NUS
Undergraduate degree with at least Second Class Honours (Upper division) / Honours (Distinction) or equivalent
Must be offered admission to a full-time graduate research programme at NUS at the time of award
Must be eligible for the MOE tuition fee subsidy
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to PhD and Master's (Research) candidates at NUS. Applicants must hold an undergraduate degree with at least Second Class Honours (Upper division) / Honours (Distinction) or equivalent, must have been offered admission to a full-time graduate research programme at NUS, and must be eligible for the MOE tuition-fee subsidy. Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents and all international students may apply.
benefits: PhD stipend: SGD 3,800/month (Singapore Citizen), SGD 3,400/month (Singapore Permanent Resident), SGD 3,000/month (international student)
Master's (Research) stipend: SGD 3,800/month (Singapore Citizen), SGD 3,000/month (Singapore Permanent Resident), SGD 2,900/month (international student)
Increased PhD stipend of SGD 500/month after passing the PhD Qualifying Examination
CPF contributions on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens
coverage: Full waiver of tuition fees at the University
Additional stipend of up to SGD 500 per month after passing the PhD Qualifying Examination (PhD candidates only)
CPF contributions on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens
requirements: A good GPA in a relevant bachelor's or master's degree
A well-crafted statement of purpose detailing research interests, career aspirations and motivations
Letters of recommendation from academic or professional referees
A comprehensive CV highlighting academic accomplishments and pertinent experience
documents: Good GPA in a relevant bachelor's or master's degree
Well-crafted statement of purpose detailing research interests, career aspirations and motivations
Letters of recommendation from academic or professional referees
Comprehensive CV highlighting academic accomplishments and pertinent experience
Standardized test scores such as the GRE (optional)
Publications or involvement in research projects (optional)
TOEFL or IELTS proficiency evidence for non-native English speakers (optional)
existing.english_requirement: For non-native English speakers, proficiency demonstrated through tests like TOEFL or IELTS (listed as an optional supporting item on the official page).
application_method: Apply for the scholarship within the NUS graduate admissions application through GradApp
Fulfil the additional scholarship application requirements stated in GradApp
Incoming graduate students should indicate their interest in the Scholarship in their admission application
existing.selection_notes: The Scholarship is tenable for one year in the first instance and thereafter may, subject to the Scholar's satisfactory progress, be renewed each semester at the University's discretion. The maximum period is two years for Master's candidates and four years for PhD candidates, as determined by the relevant faculty or school.
existing.best_fit: New or continuing NUS research master's or PhD candidates with a strong academic record who need full tuition coverage plus a living stipend; international candidates should budget for the Graduate Assistantship Programme teaching commitment.
existing.notes: Stipend rates shown are the international-student rates because this row targets international applicants; the official page publishes different rates by citizenship status. The award is a full tuition waiver plus a stipend, but international scholars must serve the Graduate Assistantship Programme, so it is not an unconditional grant.
existing.duration: Typical award period 4 years for PhD students and 2 years for Master's (Research) students; tenable for one year in the first instance and renewable each semester.
existing.application_period: Applied for within the NUS graduate admissions application (GradApp) for the August (Semester 1) or January (Semester 2) research intake; the scholarship is awarded each semester.
existing.deadline_display: No scholarship-specific deadline is published. The official page lists the application windows as "August (Semester 1 Intake) - Please refer to faculty websites for respective application deadlines" and "January (Semester 2 Intake) - Please refer to faculty websites for respective application deadlines".
